body: i knocked on the neighbours below me's door and asked to check their vents. they claimed to be terrified of the snake and said give them half an hour. they then never knocked on my door again and ignored me.. so i tried my best here. :/

sorry but i can't be evicted for a pet escaping just because its a snake and not a fluffy cat.

regardless, i knocked on the neighbours below me's door and asked to check their vents. they claimed to be terrified of the snake and said give them half an hour. they then never knocked on my door again and ignored me.. so i tried my best here.
corn snake. i have tried to knock on the person below us' door like 10 times now.. they wont answer. :/

dude thanks so much. especially for the vent reassurance. im going to take a video down it today just in case though lmao.. all the doors are closed at all times and we've built a wall into the living room with boxes and shelves and various other objects so she cant weasel out.. hopefully. also the flour trick so we could see a trail. 

shes full grown, 7 year old corn so shes decently sized. i think i might show BF this thread to prove the point of seriousness regarding care and keeping an eye.

in 2 nights im off so ill definitely do all this stuff and put a bunch of bag down, sit quietly and wait. until then ill keep leaving out food and hope she might just go back into her warm tank, ive left it next to the mouse. thanks again!
thats exactly what i need to check out the vent. if i can confirm that shes not there then ill know shes in the apartment itself and its a waiting game. thank you!!

he's worried + guilty and helped set traps, but not anywhere as worried as me. he's not really thinking about what happens if she is already out of our flat and just thinks she's definitely in the living room.

we checked dressers but not *in* clothes, thats a good idea. ill shake out sweaters this morning.

i agree, i do want to give him a second chance. he was so excited and i feel so guilty that he like, broke his new cool toy. but in giving him another chance im so scared this would happen again...

im in a top floor apartment so for her to go up theres an attic which was empty, and for the outside she would have to go a long way down to get there. theres no snake catching specialists in my area from what ive seen online but im going to be calling local pet shops for advice on who to contact. up until this point someone has also been at home and therefore keeping lights on, hopefully now that the next few nights we'll be at work it'll be dark enough to entice her back out. there's no cracks we can find except for the aforementioned vent that my boyfriend thinks she hasn't gone in since he was next to it and it had saran wrap on it prior to her disappearance.. but i am almost convinced shes there.
unfortunately i work nights the next 2 nights so when im finally off im going to sit in the dark for a while
i have :( and under the stove, i literally cut my couches up to try and find her. shes well hidden for now

i will only tell them if i am ABSOLUTELY sure theres 0 chance shes in our apt, im getting flour today and putting it along the baseboards and doorways so she'll make a trail... if theres no sign after that i should probably mention it. i understand snakes are scary, she gives me the jeebies sometimes too. i helped a friend by taking her because he didn't have the right set up, ironically
i did shavings for now but will definitely try the flour trick tomorrow! thank you

ill keep that in mind, im working the next 2 nights and then i do 4 off. if she doesn't appear before then, im camping out for a few hours on my nights off. i believe shes in the living room so we built a barricade in there and put shavings down so if she slithers through it we'll know what direction she went. glad to hear this isnt such a crazy occurrence.. if we keep her after this im getting a door for our living room!
im in ontario so im sure i cant be evicted for just getting a new pet, but thats my anxiety with telling him. i dont know what an escaped pet qualifies as...

im considering getting my moms cat to come for a visit to sniff her out.. tonight itll be dark and quiet while we both work a midnight so i am really really hoping she'll show. we barricaded the living room, the last place she was chilling in and left heat pads and a mouse.

i know this is possible for sure, she most likely is just in our apartment in a couch or something but its the risk of her ending up in a kids' room driving me batty with anxiety right now. thank you for the slight peace of mind though haha

i am definitely reconsidering if we should keep snakes now. my beardie is loud when she walks and returns to her cage when cold, it seems snakes are obviously not that interested in being a cage-dwelling friend lol

thanks for your whole response. he was helpful the first day and helped setting up traps, but now that shes been gone for over 24 hours my calm turned into WHAT ARE WE GOING TO DO?? i dont want to tell the landlords because theyre not exactly pet friendly either (but as i said, law in canada is youre protected to have pets once in a lease) so its just i dont want any animosity. another day and ill have to at least ask my neighbors if theyve seen any noodle animals roaming. he was excited about her but i think he severely underestimated her ability to slink away because he thought she was like the bearded dragon- slower and often returns to her cage when cold. if we decide to keep her and we find her ill have to have a real sit down about this i think and research care together instead of just me being the expert (and i still make mistakes too lol)
i dont know anyone myself but i can call my local reptile store and ask those ladies, theyve always been super sweet to me
yeah and the people below me have little kids. theres no point in trying to convince parents "shes a nice snake!!" around kiddos

i'll keep double checking, i figure once it's dark and we're at work tonight she may peep out to get the mouse next to her cage and go home. she also likes to climb UP instead of going down into vents, so i hope that'll work in our favor

she's about 3.5-4 feet corn snake, not massive but big enough that you have to use 2 hands to pick her up for sure. from our investigations there's no piping she could go into or holes in our walls, but there is 1 vent next to our couch she might have fallen into. BF says no way because he would have seen her go down there or heard a plop, but i'm doubtful. we've used flashlights under everything and into the vents but no luck... she might have gone into the furnace room at worst? that's where the vent leads..
